source_text: Ὁ δὲ μακάριος Πόθεινος, ὁ τὴν διακονίαν τῆς ἐπισκοπῆς ἐν Λουγδούνῳ πεπιστευμένος, ὑπὲρ τὰ ἐνενήκοντα ἔτη τῆς ἡλικίας γεγονώς, καὶ πάνυ ἀσθενὴς τῷ σώματι, μόλις μὲν ἐμπνέων διὰ τὴν προκειμένην σωματικὴν ἀσθένειαν, ὑπὸ δὲ προθυμίας πνεύματος ἀναρρωννύμενος διὰ τὴν ἐγκειμένην τῆς μαρτυρίας ἐπιθυμίαν, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπὶ τὸ βῆμα ἐσύρετο, τοῦ μὲν σώματος καὶ ὑπὸ τοῦ γήρως καὶ ὑπὸ τῆς νόσου λελυμένου, τηρουμένης δὲ τῆς ψυχῆς ἐν αὐτῷ, ἵνα δι᾽ αὐτῆς Χριστὸς θριαμβεύσῃ· ὃς ὑπὸ τῶν στρατιωτῶν ἐπὶ τὸ βῆμα κομισθείς, παραπεμπόντων αὐτὸν τῶν πολιτικῶν ἐξουσιῶν καὶ παντὸς τοῦ πλήθους, ἐπιβοήσεις παντοίας ποιουμένων ὡς αὐτοῦ ὄντος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἀπεδίδου τὴν καλὴν μαρτυρίαν. Ἀνεταζόμενος δὲ ὑπὸ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος τίς εἴη Χριστιανῶν ὁ θεός, ἔφη· Ἐὰν ᾖς ἄξιος, γνώσῃ. Ἐντεῦθεν δὲ ἀφειδῶς ἐσύρετο καὶ ποικίλας ἔπασχε πληγάς, τῶν μὲν σύνεγγυς χερσὶν καὶ ποσὶν ἐνυβριζόντων παντοίως, μηδὲ τὴν ἡλικίαν αἰδουμένων αὐτοῦ, τῶν δὲ μακράν, ὃ μετὰ χεῖρας ἕκαστος εἶχεν, εἰς αὐτὸν ἀκοντιζόντων, πάντων δὲ ἡγουμένων μεγάλως πλημμελεῖν καὶ ἀσεβεῖν, εἴ τις ἀπολειφθείη τῆς εἰς αὐτὸν ἀσελγείας· καὶ γὰρ τοὺς θεοὺς αὐτῶν ᾤοντο οὕτως ἐκδικήσειν. Καὶ μόγις ἐμπνέων ἐρρίφη ἐν τῇ εἱρκτῇ καὶ μετὰ δύο ἡμέρας ἐξέπνευσεν.
thought_title: An old bishop dragged before the tribunal and dying in prison
orientation: After deaths from prison confinement, the narrative turns to Pothinus, bishop of Lyons, being brought before the governor.
pass_a_gloss: But the blessed Pothinus, the one entrusted with the service of the bishop office in Lyons, having come to be beyond ninety years of age, and very weak in the body, barely breathing on the one hand because of the bodily weakness set before him, but being made strong again on the other hand by eagerness of spirit because of the desire for witness pressing upon him, even he himself was dragged to the tribunal, with the body on the one hand loosened both by old age and by sickness, but with the soul being kept in him, in order that through it Christ might triumph. He, carried to the tribunal by the soldiers, while the city authorities and all the crowd accompanied him, making all kinds of shouts as if he himself were the Christ, rendered the good witness. And while being questioned by the governor who might be the god of the Christians, he said: If you are worthy, you will know. From that point he was dragged without sparing and suffered varied blows, with those near at hand insulting him in every way with hands and feet, not even respecting his age, and those far off hurling at him whatever each had in his hands, and all judging that they would greatly offend and act impiously if anyone fell short in outrage against him; for in this way they thought they would avenge their own gods. And barely breathing he was thrown into the prison and after two days he breathed out.

pass_b_english: Blessed Pothinus, who had been entrusted with the bishop's office in Lyons, was over ninety years old and very weak in body. He could scarcely breathe because of his physical illness, but eagerness of spirit gave him strength again because of his urgent desire for witness. He too was dragged to the tribunal, his body broken down by both age and sickness, while his soul was still kept within him so that Christ might triumph through it. Soldiers carried him to the tribunal, with the city authorities and the whole crowd escorting him and raising all kinds of shouts against him as though he himself were Christ. There he bore his good witness.

When the governor asked him who is the God of the Christians, Pothinus said, "If you are worthy, you will know." After that he was dragged without mercy and suffered many kinds of blows. Those standing near abused him in every way with hands and feet, showing no respect for his age, while those farther off hurled at him whatever each had in hand. All of them believed it a grave fault and impiety to fall short in outrage against him, for they thought they were avenging their gods in this way. Still barely breathing, he was thrown into prison and died two days later.
